purpose: Power Stack story map. Themes decide what deserves research; they do not automatically raise a company score. Each theme should explain the money chain, the investable bottleneck and what would prove the story wrong.

environment.label: Near-record US indices, weaker AI chips, still-expensive long-term finance.
environment.summary: 13 October US close: S&P 500 7,805.45 (-0.02%), Nasdaq 27,204.38 (-0.15%), SMH 588.12 (-0.49%). The AI buildout remains real, but China/CXMT memory competition and expensive financing are making the chip trade less forgiving. US10Y ~5.216% in 13 October financial-market reporting; CPI on 14 October and TSMC Q3 on 15 October are next tests. Power Stack treats this as a selective early-warning market, not a proven collapse.

whatIsNewNow: 13 Oct close: S&P 500 slipped 0.02%, Nasdaq 0.15% and SMH 0.49%. Semiconductor selling is outpacing the broader market; check earnings/orders and not only the AI growth story.

Eisman financing-chain warning is a research hypothesis: big cloud RPO/capex and circular venture sponsorship require independently paid demand, cash conversion and comparable net lab revenue. Microsoft positive FCF and strong power/electrical backlogs are bullish counterevidence.

Agriculture map reset: Corteva completed the Vylor separation on 1 October, so the old CTVA seed/genetics thesis is no longer valid. Seed/genetics research moves to VYLR; CTVA must be re-underwritten as crop protection.

Google has now turned AI power scarcity into contracted infrastructure: 3.59 GW with Constellation, including 890 MW of nuclear power for 20 years, with more than $4.3B of fleet investment tied to the deal.

Black Hills plans $1.8B of generation investment for a proposed Google data centre. Named hyperscaler load is starting to underwrite utility-style capex rather than merely compete for existing grid capacity.
The credit market is becoming two-speed. Weak borrowers are facing punitive refinancing costs, while strong sponsor-backed AI infrastructure can still raise record-scale financing.

US equities have remained resilient enough for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to trade at records as long yields eased from their peaks. This is real earnings/AI resilience, not proof that expensive money no longer matters.

Gulf crude and condensate flows have recovered much faster than refined products. The remaining energy risk is increasingly diesel/jet/LPG, logistics, replacement-barrel premiums and vulnerable infrastructure rather than a simple shortage of crude.
Chinese refiners are paying large premiums for substitute Iraqi/Qatari barrels as Iranian flows fall, which keeps feedstock and product costs elevated even when headline crude availability improves.

The latest creator transcripts reinforce useful questions around narrow breadth, offshore dollar funding, white-collar labour weakness and gold versus yields, but those claims remain zero-weight until independently verified.

The strongest investable change is upstream of compute: operating generation, contracted power, grid equipment and interconnection now have direct customer-backed evidence rather than only thematic demand.
whatMattersMostToMarketsNow: AI commitments versus paid end-customer cash; issuer FCF, leases, customer concentration and verified debt distribution
Long-end real yields, term premium and whether credit stress broadens beyond weak borrowers
Customer-backed AI power procurement and funded generation/grid capex
AI financing quality, sponsor strength and cash conversion
Breadth beyond AI/semiconductors and whether record indices can survive renewed yield pressure
Refined-product, logistics and infrastructure risk rather than crude price alone
US–China AI price war, inference growth and compute/memory sovereignty
Verified labour/consumer weakness beneath headline employment

themes.name: Expensive Money Is the Market Hurdle
themes.whyNow: High rates are not shutting capital equally. Weak borrowers are seeing punitive refinancing costs, while strong sponsor-backed AI infrastructure can still raise tens of billions. The hurdle is now who can fund growth without giving away the economics.
themes.marketTransmission: high risk-free rate → weak borrowers reprice first → strong sponsors and contracted projects keep funding → valuation and capex outcomes diverge
themes.confirmation: long yields stay restrictive while weak-credit refinancing costs remain punitive and sponsor-backed infrastructure continues to clear financing
themes.invalidation: broad credit spreads tighten materially, refinancing costs fall and weaker borrowers regain easy access to capital
themes.nextTest: 2Y/5Y/10Y/20Y/30Y yields, HY/IG spreads, refinancing calendars and whether strong-project financing remains distributable.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Prefer cash generators, named customers and contracted offtake. Penalise businesses that need cheap refinancing or speculative project finance.

themes.name: AI Still Needs the Physical Stuff
themes.whyNow: Steve Eisman's financing warning adds a crucial question to strong power and equipment demand: are the named projects actually funded by external paying customers? GEV and ETN have disclosed operating backlogs, but even picks-and-shovels orders may be deferred if lab commitments are not collected. Chip shares fell in the 13 Oct session while wider US indices barely moved.
themes.marketTransmission: AI lab commitments and funded data centres create turbine, grid, electrical and cooling orders; actual project cash receipts turn backlog into earnings. Cheaper models may raise usage, but financing delays can interrupt delivery.
themes.confirmation: Named, creditworthy customer funding; deposits/interconnection; delivered generation and electrical backlog converted to improving free cash flow
themes.invalidation: Material project cancellations, postponed grid links, cancelled turbine/electrical orders, backlog margin erosion or weak collection despite growth
themes.nextTest: GEV/ETN/VRT order-to-cash conversion and customer concentration; TSMC 15 Oct to test hardware demand; debt funding and power interconnection
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: GEV/ETN remain scored no-chase entry studies, VRT stays unscored research; do not promote ANET/CSCO without issuer underwriting and price/valuation.

themes.name: Who Is Financing the AI Boom?
themes.whyNow: Eisman's concentration thesis highlights the dependence of future cloud revenue on OpenAI/Anthropic payments. Nvidia's five direct receivables customers represented ~70% in its July 2026 10-Q; Oracle's $664B RPO is future contracted revenue, not cash. Microsoft's reported positive $19.6B FY2026 Q4 FCF is a crucial bullish exception. The interview's claim that two labs represent 70% of hyperscaler AI revenue is unverified on common denominators.
themes.marketTransmission: AI lab paid users → lab cash/financing → actual cloud payment → hyperscaler cash capex/leases → GPU, network and power supplier orders; concentration/funding gaps can force cuts before broad AI adoption stops
themes.confirmation: Signed outside-lab paying customer contracts; comparable net revenue and improving cash margins; closed financing and sustained supplier orders without vendor-funded demand
themes.invalidation: Verified funding failure or poor cash collections followed by delayed payments/orders, weak utilisation, earnings cuts and widening issuer credit spreads
themes.nextTest: OpenAI/Anthropic net paying revenue and funding closes; Oracle RPO conversion/deposits; Nvidia receivables; Microsoft/AWS/Google cash capex, leases and FCF; Meta lease obligations; borrower spreads
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Keep AVGO conditional and ORCL/CRWV as risk comparators; favour independently paid orders and FCF. Do not mechanically change scores or declare a bubble pop from creator testimony.

themes.name: Diesel and LNG Can Keep Inflation Sticky
themes.whyNow: Headline Gulf crude availability is improving, but refined-product exports, replacement-barrel costs, refinery economics and infrastructure risk are not normal yet. The inflation tail is moving from missing crude toward diesel/jet/LPG, logistics and physical disruption.
themes.marketTransmission: fuel/logistics scarcity → freight and power costs → margins and inflation → fewer rate cuts
themes.confirmation: distillate inventories/cracks and freight stay elevated independently of crude
themes.invalidation: product inventories rebuild and cracks/freight normalize together
themes.nextTest: EIA product inventories, ULSD/RBOB cracks, refinery utilisation, Gulf storm shut-ins, substitute-barrel premiums and refined-product export recovery
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Keep XOM/LNG as higher-quality cash generators; VLO/STNG remain selective product/logistics expressions. Do not rerate generic upstream beta just because oil headlines rise.

themes.name: Memory and Interconnect Are the AI Bottleneck
themes.whyNow: CXMT progress increases competitive questions for memory and adds risk of future lower selling prices. SMH closed 13 October at 588.12 (-0.49%), underperforming the broad US indices; this is price weakness, not proof of cancelled HBM orders. Look past GPU headlines to the economics of HBM, fibre/network switches and booked cash margins.
themes.marketTransmission: larger AI clusters → more memory bandwidth + faster links → pricing power for scarce components
themes.confirmation: Current HBM contract pricing/utilisation and interconnect/network orders hold up after current China news; cash conversion and customer diversification improve
themes.invalidation: HBM mix/pricing falls, verified orders roll over, inventory rises or customer-concentration plus lower expected earnings undermines multiples
themes.nextTest: TSMC Q3 15 Oct, Micron memory/HBM contract evidence, ANET AI networking revenue and repeat order quality, CRDO customer concentration; compare chip performance against QQQ
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: MU remains scored but no-blind-chase; ANET/CSCO are unscored supplier research leads, CRDO remains an existing high-ranked candidate.

themes.name: Cheaper AI Makes the Hardware War Bigger
themes.whyNow: Chinese labs are pushing model prices down while China is also trying to localise the hardware stack. Cheaper models can hurt software economics but expand usage, which can increase demand for memory, interconnect and domestic semiconductor capacity.
themes.marketTransmission: model price ↓ → inference ↑ → hardware traffic ↑; export controls → localisation spend ↑
themes.confirmation: Chinese AI/cloud usage and CSP capex keep rising while memory/interconnect demand remains strong and domestic semiconductor qualification/localisation advances
themes.invalidation: inference growth fails to offset falling model prices, Chinese CSP capex rolls over, or memory/interconnect supply normalises faster than workload growth
themes.nextTest: Alibaba AI-cloud growth versus capex; CXMT HBM/customer qualification; Montage CXL adoption; Innolight optical orders; Chinese CSP capex and semiconductor-equipment localisation
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Separate beneficiaries of more AI usage from companies that merely have an AI label. Verify CXMT/HBM progress before treating it like proven MU economics.

themes.name: Critical Minerals / Rare Earth / Copper Supply Security
themes.whyNow: The US-China truce extension did not verify resolution of rare-earth access. Yttrium bottlenecks remain strategically relevant to jet engines, power equipment and semiconductor manufacturing while copper/electrical demand stays tied to grid buildout.
themes.marketTransmission: aerospace, semiconductors, power equipment, defense, electrification capex, commodity pricing
themes.confirmation: persistent physical tightness, strategic procurement/offtake and supply diversification investment
themes.invalidation: verified durable export normalization plus falling physical premia/inventories rebuilding
themes.nextTest: rare-earth/yttrium export data, government procurement, copper inventories and grid demand
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: FCX remains active at disciplined prices; avoid conflating strategic scarcity with automatic miner upside

themes.name: AI Security / Governance
themes.whyNow: Commercial AI-security products and governance/evaluation services are turning the theme into recurring-spend mechanisms rather than generic AI fear. The challenge is valuation after strong price moves.
themes.marketTransmission: cybersecurity budgets, recurring ARR, model testing/governance, enterprise software mix
themes.confirmation: ARR/bookings, renewals and AI-security attach rates accelerate
themes.invalidation: spend remains experimental, low-value or commoditized
themes.nextTest: bookings, renewal economics and AI-security product adoption
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: keep PANW/CRWD high quality; wait for price rather than chase

themes.name: US LNG Diversification / Energy Security
themes.whyNow: Diversification from vulnerable supply routes remains structurally important, but the latest US-China meeting did not produce a verified LNG breakthrough and the immediate market is dominated by rates and refined products.
themes.marketTransmission: US gas, LNG contracting, Europe/Asia gas security, shipping
themes.confirmation: new SPAs, high utilization and durable international demand
themes.invalidation: weak contracting plus normalized competing supply/routes
themes.nextTest: new SPA/offtake announcements and China market access
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: LNG remains a high-quality entry candidate; no urgency chase

themes.name: Agriculture / Fertilizer / Food Affordability
themes.whyNow: The old agriculture map changed structurally on 1 October when Corteva separated its seed/genetics business into Vylor. CF is producing strong cash in a constructive nitrogen market, Nutrien reported record first-half potash volumes and lower capex guidance, while Bunge raised its full-year EPS outlook. Agriculture is a real portfolio diversifier, but the preferred vehicle must now be re-selected.
themes.marketTransmission: farm income and crop/input ratios → seed/trait demand, nitrogen/potash application, crop-protection volumes and processing margins
themes.confirmation: VYLR proves standalone seed economics, CF/NTR maintain cash conversion and farmer affordability does not force broad input cuts
themes.invalidation: farm economics deteriorate enough to cut seed/input volumes broadly or the post-spin businesses fail to convert margins into cash
themes.nextTest: VYLR Form 10/first standalone results, New Corteva post-spin margins, CF nitrogen pricing/gas costs, NTR potash pricing/volumes and Bunge/Viterra integration
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: VYLR becomes the seed/genetics research target; New CTVA must be rebuilt as crop protection; CF is the strongest current cash case; NTR is secondary; BG remains background rather than stop-looking.

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel
themes.whyNow: Strategic baseload/fuel-cycle thesis remains intact, but no new contracting catalyst currently outranks rates, products or AI/grid. CCJ's falling tape improves valuation but still needs stabilization.
themes.marketTransmission: uranium contracting, conversion/enrichment, baseload power and data-centre power planning
themes.confirmation: long-term contracting, enrichment/conversion awards and project execution
themes.invalidation: utility contracting weakens materially or supply normalizes faster than demand
themes.nextTest: utility contracting/fuel-cycle awards and CCJ price stabilization
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CCJ stays quality nuclear exposure but wait for a base/reclaim before increasing priority

themes.name: Precious Metals
themes.whyNow: Gold remains structurally supported by fiscal/geopolitical risk but is down on the week as the dollar and long yields rise. The current tape says rates dominate the hedge bid at the margin.
themes.marketTransmission: real/nominal yields, USD, fiscal risk, positioning
themes.confirmation: DXY and real/nominal yields roll over together while gold reclaims recent resistance
themes.nextTest: Treasury/Fed follow-through and gold response around recent support
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: no chase; wait for rate confirmation

themes.name: Robotics / Automation
themes.whyNow: Evidence still favors conventional industrial/warehouse automation and cobots over general-purpose humanoids. Chinese regulators are applying more discipline to humanoid IPOs while installed volumes remain small versus standard industrial robots.
themes.marketTransmission: industrial capex, warehouse productivity, machine vision, motion control, sensors, semiconductor equipment
themes.confirmation: repeat orders, utilization, margins and scaled commercial deployments
themes.nextTest: industrial orders and Hong Kong pricing/trading for new automation listings
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: favor profitable fixed/warehouse automation; RoboTechnik/humanoids research-only until pricing and economics prove out

themes.name: Grid ESS vs Lithium Overcapacity
themes.whyNow: Grid storage deployment is real, but generic cell/miner economics remain burdened by excess capacity. Downstream storage economics remain more investable than broad lithium beta.
themes.marketTransmission: BESS deployment, cell pricing, lithium margins, grid balancing
themes.confirmation: storage backlog, utilization and margins improve
themes.invalidation: deployment slows while cell/miner oversupply persists
themes.nextTest: storage bookings, margins and cell pricing
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: TSLA storage is the clearest bridge; generic lithium remains background
